title: Longest run of the same number
scenario: A shelf of numbered balls, in a jumble. Line them up in order — then what's the longest run of the same number sitting together?

intro.job: A shelf of numbered balls, in a jumble. Line them up in order — then what's the longest run of the same number sitting together?

idea.rule: Sort first, then count the runs — equal numbers only sit together after sorting.
idea.detail: Two patterns chained: sorting (013) lines the numbers up so equal ones sit together; best-so-far tracking (045) remembers the longest run seen. The draft counts runs without sorting, so the 3s split into a run of two and a run of three — and the real run of five never appears.

model_restatement: Line the balls up in order, then find the longest run of the same number — and print its length.

clarify.question: What if no number repeats?
clarify.answer: Then every run is 1 — the answer is 1.

clarify.question: Why sort first?
clarify.answer: Runs only sit together after sorting — unsorted, the same number's copies split into separate runs.

clarify.question: What counts as a run?
clarify.answer: Equal numbers sitting next to each other — 3, 3, 3 is a run of three.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Sort the numbers. Walk them, counting the current run. Remember the longest run. Print it.

checkpoints.prompt: The second run of 3s — how long is it now?
On the print line, what is best?
With the fix — after the last number, what is best?

why_line: The draft counts runs on the jumbled shelf: the 3s sit in two separate runs of two and three, so the longest run it ever sees is 3 — the run of five only exists after sorting.

explain.rule: Runs only exist where equal numbers sit together — count on a jumbled list and the runs split.
explain.bridge: Where do the 3s sit — together in one run, or split across the shelf?

fix.rule: Sort first, then count: nums = sorted(nums) before the loop.

walk.gloss: Sort the numbers — equal ones sit together now.
Same as the last one? The run grows.
Remember the longest run so far.
Different number — start a fresh run.

contrast.wrong: count runs on the jumbled list

alternatives.note: Count each value's copies — the biggest count is the longest run.

hints: Where do the equal numbers sit?
The runs split on a jumbled list — line them up first.
nums = sorted(nums) — then count the runs.

follow_up.prompt: One more shelf: [4, 4, 1, 4, 4, 4, 4] — what's the longest run?

checkpoint.prompt: With the new shelf, what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — sorting lines the 4s up, whatever the shelf is.

one_liner: Sort first, then count the runs — equal numbers only sit together after sorting.
